correctness.rationale: The neighborhood parity equations are equivalent to the six-dimensional Fibonacci recurrence with both zero boundary columns. Over F2, the characteristic polynomial is (x^3+x+1)^2; f9(B)=0, while f1(B) through f8(B) are invertible by their nonzero residues modulo irreducible x^3+x+1. T^9=diag(B^7,B^7) makes all solutions periodic in blocks of nine, and a zero-column reflection repeats the eight-column support weight q times. All 64 possible six-bit initial columns are classified explicitly by a disjoint table, yielding the claimed exact coefficients. Independently reconstructed binary Gaussian elimination confirms all lengths 1–54 and direct parity-tested recurrence confirms 1–144; the infinite statement rests on the proof, not finite sampling.

value.rationale: The explicit first nontrivial six-row nullspace primitive is mathematically motivated by the 2002 recurrence and 2026 nullspace-prime research. The all-width result determines a complete new natural invariant, including eight nonzero weight levels, sharp minimum support 18q with four minimizers, and exact silent-press probabilities for biased random moves. This is not supplied by nullity tables or generic existence theorems; the six-row family is natural, and the exact eight-column census gives an auditable nontrivial refinement.
